nodes.label: Cash-account loss diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Diagnoses one frozen FTFT opportunity, its signal, target geometry, admission funnel, selection rule and execution costs without a new strategy replay or parameter search.

nodes.label: FTFT September 14 breakout reversal
nodes.rationale: Fifty shares entered at $4.951 and exited at $4.579 after the $4.59 stop, losing $18.70. No holding-period quote reached the $5.68 target; the $5.23 high was a conditional mark with limited displayed capacity. Price movement dominated the loss, while delayed execution and costs further reduced proceeds.

nodes.label: Momentum score 85 and entry extension
nodes.rationale: The confirmed score of 85 followed a 30.32% five-minute rise and 20.50% extension above VWAP. RSI 76.31 removed points rather than vetoing entry. The score is a weighted checklist, not an 85% success probability; the last prefill score remained eligible at 90, so stale-signal failure was not established.

nodes.label: ATR payoff geometry versus hit probability
nodes.rationale: ATR $0.23465 and the rounded 1.5-ATR stop produced about 7.29% downside and a 2R target requiring about 14.72% upside within fifteen minutes. These equations define price distances, not probabilities or arrival times, so nominal reward/risk alone cannot establish positive expected profit.

nodes.label: Empty admissible entry-price interval
nodes.rationale: Twenty-seven of 71 alerts were structurally rejected when one-cent rounding and a 0.25-ATR chase allowance made cap equal trigger despite positive displacement. All had ATR below $0.04. The example requires ask >= $4.49 and ask <= $4.489; rejecting it is correct, while price-grid compatibility remains a research assumption. Funnel blockers overlap and do not imply rejected opportunities would profit.

nodes.label: First feasible confirmed-alert selection
nodes.rationale: The single-entry rule chooses the first feasible alert chronologically with alphabetical ties, rather than estimating expected return. It blocked 21 later alerts despite $752.40 of unused settled cash. Two later trades improved variant A by $7.674 on this day, but one-day evidence does not establish a superior selection policy.
